'''Christopher David Godsil''' is a [[professor]] and the former Chair at the Department of [[Combinatorics]] and [[mathematical optimization|Optimization]] in the [[University of Waterloo Faculty of Mathematics|faculty of mathematics]] at the [[University of Waterloo]]. He wrote the popular textbook on [[algebraic graph&nbsp;theory]], entitled ''Algebraic Graph&nbsp;Theory'', with [[Gordon Royle]],<ref>[[Robin Wilson (mathematician)|Robin J. Wilson]]'s review of {{harvtxt|Godsil|Royle|2004}} for ''[[Mathematical Reviews]]'' ({{MR|1829620}}).</ref> His earlier textbook on [[algebraic combinatorics]] discussed  [[distance-regular graph]]s and [[association&nbsp;scheme]]s.<ref>Andrew Woldar's review of {{harvtxt|Godsil|1993}} for ''Mathematical Reviews'' ({{MR|1220704}}).</ref>

==Background==

He started the [[Journal of Algebraic Combinatorics]], and was an Editor-in-Chief of the [[Electronic Journal of Combinatorics]] from 2004 to 2008. He is also on the editorial board of the [[Journal of Combinatorial Theory]] Series&nbsp;B and [[Combinatorica]].<ref>[http://quoll.uwaterloo.ca/me/cv.html Chris Godsil's CV] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100514161053/http://quoll.uwaterloo.ca/me/cv.html |date=May 14, 2010 }}.</ref>

He obtained his [[Ph.D.]] in 1979 at the [[University of Melbourne]] under the supervision of Derek&nbsp;Alan Holton.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=17957}}.</ref> He wrote a paper with [[Paul Erdős]], so making his [[Erdős number]] equal to&nbsp;1.<ref>[[Paul Erdős]], Chris&nbsp;D. Godsil, S.&nbsp;G. Krantz, and [[Torrence Parsons|T.&nbsp;D. Parsons]], "Intersection graphs for families of balls in $R\sp n$." ''European J. Combin.'' '''9'''(5), pp. 501-505, (1988).</ref>
